title: Indus Valley Civilization found by railway workers
place_text: Mohenjo-daro and Harappa, Indus River, Pakistan

tellings.quote: accidental Discovery uh Railway workers building a railway line that actually led to that

plain: The Indus Valley Civilization was an ancient culture whose ruined cities, Mohenjo-daro and Harappa, lie along the Indus River in what is now Pakistan. A writer on lost ancient civilizations, Graham Hancock, told podcast host Jesse Michels that it was found in the 1920s by accident, when railway workers laying a line came across the remains. He tells it to show how whole civilizations can stay hidden until luck turns them up.
